Summary

TCGA-KIRC: Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma (methylation, 50 samples), 50 samples was analysed with the DNA methylation arrays workflow (version 1.0.0) on the LSMA Analysis Lab. To find which positions differ between 'tumour' and 'normal' (column 'tissue'), adjusting for patient. In summary, 68,925 positions passed the thresholds. 4 point(s) are flagged under Limitations and should be read before the results are used.

  • 68,925 positions passed the thresholds.

Introduction

From Illumina 450K or EPIC array data (raw IDAT files or a table of beta values) to quality control, exploration, differentially methylated positions and regions, and gene-set analysis. Human samples only. The data analysed here is of kind 'methyl_beta'.

Aim

To find which positions differ between 'tumour' and 'normal' (column 'tissue'), adjusting for patient.

Source: TCGA project TCGA-KIRC (Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma), open-access files from the NCI Genomic Data Commons. Beta values from the GDC's uniform pipeline (SeSAMe). Probes that SeSAMe masks have no value. 50 of 483 samples (25 Primary Tumor, 25 Solid Tissue Normal); 421,261 probes with a value in at least one sample. https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/projects/TCGA-KIRC Cite the TCGA Research Network and the marker paper of this project.

Methods

Assembled from what each completed stage recorded. Check it against the parameter tables below before using it in a write-up.

DNA methylation of 50 human samples was measured on the Infinium HumanMethylation450 (450K) array (TCGA-KIRC_methylation_beta_values.tsv.gz); 421,037 probes were read. Normalisation: none applied here: the values are used as the authors normalised them. Positions refer to hg19 (GRCh37).

Of 50 uploaded samples, 50 took part in the comparison of 'tissue' (normal, tumour); 0 samples were excluded by the analyst for the reasons listed under Data input, 0 belonged to no compared group, and the group label of 0 sample(s) was harmonised before analysis.

Probes were filtered (missing values: 59,701; not a CpG probe: 1,440; sex chromosome: 7,511; common SNP at the CpG: 1,349), leaving 351,036 of 421,037. Cross-reactive probes: not removed (no list of cross-reactive probes is installed).

Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering (complete linkage, Euclidean distance) used the 5,000 most variable probes on the M-value scale.

Differentially methylated positions were tested with limma (empirical Bayes moderated t-test on M-values; difference reported on the beta scale) using the design ~ tissue + patient for the contrast tumour vs normal. P-values were adjusted with the BH method; CpGs with adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute difference in beta of at least 0.1 were called.

Differentially methylated regions were identified with DMRcate (Gaussian kernel smoothing of the limma statistics along the genome) (lambda = 1000 bp, C = 2, FDR 0.05), keeping regions with at least 3 CpGs and a mean absolute difference in beta of at least 0.05.

Gene sets were tested with missMethyl::gsameth (Wallenius' noncentral hypergeometric test, corrected for probe number and multi-gene probes) on all CpGs, separately for hyper and hypo CpGs; background: all 351,036 CpGs tested for differential methylation. Gene sets were taken from MSigDB 2026.1.Hs via msigdbr (collections: hallmark, go_bp).

Random seed: 42. Software: R 4.5.2; Bioconductor 3.21; DMRcate 3.4.1; IlluminaHumanMethylation450kanno.ilmn12.hg19 0.6.1; data.table 1.18.6.1; jsonlite 2.0.0; limma 3.64.3; matrixStats 1.5.0; missMethyl 1.42.0; msigdbr 26.1.1; org.Hs.eg.db 3.21.0.

Analyses were run on the LSMA Analysis Lab (workflow 'dna-methylation' version 1.0.0).

Results

One section per stage, in the order they ran. The badge on each heading says how far its output can be taken: exploratory output describes the data, statistically supported output carries a test, and interpretation is a reading of either.

Stage 1 of 6

Data input Exploratory

An Illumina methylation array measures, for several hundred thousand CpG sites, how much of the DNA in the sample is methylated at that site. Each site has a probe; the result per probe and sample is a beta value between 0 (no copy methylated) and 1 (every copy methylated). If you upload raw IDAT files, minfi reads the red and green intensities, corrects them and computes the beta values. If you upload a table, the beta values are used as they are. The probe names are compared with Illumina's manifest to recognise the array (450K or EPIC), and the samples are matched to the sample sheet.

Note. 224 probe(s) are not in the 450K manifest (for example control or SNP probes) and were left out.

Sample preparation

Comparison: tissue, groups normal, tumour (reference: normal). Paired by patient. Adjusted for: patient. These choices were made before the analysis and the uploaded files were not changed.

No sample was excluded by the analyst.

How to interpret this stage

Check that the array was recognised, that the number of probes is what you expect (about 485,000 for 450K, 866,000 for EPIC, fewer if the authors filtered), and that every sample found its row in the sample sheet. The median beta value per sample should be similar for samples of the same tissue.

Stage 2 of 6

Quality control and probe filtering Exploratory

Each sample is described: the distribution of its beta values, the share of probes that failed detection or are missing, and how well it correlates with the other samples. For raw arrays the overall signal and the sex predicted from the X and Y chromosomes are added. Then probes are removed that cannot be trusted: failed probes, probes on the sex chromosomes, probes with a common genetic variant at the measured site, and probes that do not measure a CpG.

Note. Flagged sample(s): TCGA-A3-3357-01A, TCGA-A3-3385-01A, TCGA-B0-4688-01A, TCGA-B0-4690-01A, TCGA-B0-4694-01A, TCGA-B0-4696-01A, TCGA-B0-4698-01A, TCGA-B0-4707-01A, TCGA-B0-4688-11A, TCGA-B0-4690-11A, TCGA-B0-4691-11A, TCGA-B0-4697-11A, TCGA-B0-4699-11A, TCGA-B0-4701-11A, TCGA-B0-4703-11A, TCGA-B0-4707-11A, TCGA-B0-4713-11A, TCGA-B0-4718-11A. Look at them in the density plot and the PCA before deciding what to do.
Note. Detection p-values are not available for a table of beta values, so probes that failed on the array can only be recognised if the authors set them to missing.

How to interpret this stage

The density plot should show two peaks for every sample, near 0 and near 1. A sample with a flat or single-peaked curve, many failed probes, low signal, or low correlation with the rest is suspect. If the predicted sex differs from the sample sheet, a sample may have been swapped. Flags prompt you to look; the platform never removes a sample for you.

How to interpret this stage

Samples of one group lying together on the first components suggest a strong, consistent difference. If samples group by a technical column instead (slide, batch, processing date) or by sex or age, include that column in the model of the next stage. A single sample far from all others should be checked against the quality-control stage.

Stage 4 of 6

Differentially methylated positions Statistically supported

For every CpG a linear model is fitted with limma and the two groups are compared with a moderated t-test, which borrows information across CpGs to stabilise the variance estimates. The test uses M-values. The size of the effect is reported as delta beta, the difference in the share of methylated DNA, estimated with the same model on beta values. P-values are corrected for the number of CpGs tested.

How to interpret this stage

A CpG is called when its adjusted p-value is below the threshold and its delta beta is at least the chosen size. Hyper means more methylation in the test group, hypo less. Look at the p-value histogram first: a flat distribution with a peak near zero is healthy. Then look at individual CpGs in the box plots: a real difference moves the whole group. Thousands of called CpGs between tissues are normal; between two treatments of the same cells, far fewer are expected.

How to interpret this stage

Trust regions with several CpGs, a consistent direction and a mean difference large enough to matter. The profile plots show the mean methylation of each group across a region; the two lines should stay apart along its length. A region overlapping a promoter is a candidate for altered gene regulation, to be checked against expression data.

Stage 6 of 6

Gene-set analysis Biological interpretation

The called CpGs are mapped to genes, and each gene set (MSigDB Hallmark, Gene Ontology, KEGG, Reactome) is tested for containing more of those genes than expected. missMethyl takes into account that genes differ greatly in the number of probes on the array and that some probes map to several genes.

Note. More than 10,000 CpGs are called (hyper, hypo); the 10,000 with the smallest p-values were used. With too many CpGs almost every gene contains one and the test loses its meaning.

How to interpret this stage

Significant sets point to processes whose genes carry more methylation changes than expected. Read them as hypotheses. Developmental and neuronal gene sets appear in many cancer comparisons because their promoters are CpG islands that gain methylation in tumours in general; that is a known pattern, not a specific finding about your samples.

Discussion

What the run amounts to, drawn from the stages that carry a judgement. Every sentence below was written by the stage that reached it; none is a later interpretation.

This run describes the data rather than testing a hypothesis about it, so there is no verdict to draw together here. The Results describe what was measured.

The run raised 4 warnings, listed with the stages that raised them. They are part of the result, not notes beside it.

Everything above was produced by DNA methylation arrays on the data named in the Data section, with the parameters recorded under each stage. The Limitations section says what this design cannot show, and should be read before any of this is quoted.

Limitations

Everything the analysis flagged about itself, gathered in one place. Each one limits what the results above can be used for.

StageWhat was flagged
Data input224 probe(s) are not in the 450K manifest (for example control or SNP probes) and were left out.
Quality control and probe filteringFlagged sample(s): TCGA-A3-3357-01A, TCGA-A3-3385-01A, TCGA-B0-4688-01A, TCGA-B0-4690-01A, TCGA-B0-4694-01A, TCGA-B0-4696-01A, TCGA-B0-4698-01A, TCGA-B0-4707-01A, TCGA-B0-4688-11A, TCGA-B0-4690-11A, TCGA-B0-4691-11A, TCGA-B0-4697-11A, TCGA-B0-4699-11A, TCGA-B0-4701-11A, TCGA-B0-4703-11A, TCGA-B0-4707-11A, TCGA-B0-4713-11A, TCGA-B0-4718-11A. Look at them in the density plot and the PCA before deciding what to do.
Quality control and probe filteringDetection p-values are not available for a table of beta values, so probes that failed on the array can only be recognised if the authors set them to missing.
Gene-set analysisMore than 10,000 CpGs are called (hyper, hypo); the 10,000 with the smallest p-values were used. With too many CpGs almost every gene contains one and the test loses its meaning.
